source.title: Computational Separation Between Convolutional and Fully-Connected Networks

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares convolutional, locally connected, and fully connected networks on synthetic local and nonlocal parity tasks built from MNIST sequences, using a different setting and measure from the image-classification comparisons in V3.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses cited prior results, which are not recorded as rows. Its own CIFAR-10 parameter-count comparison is described in the text but the figure provides no recoverable exact values; row R7 records only the stated comparison. No experiment tests random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, optimizer comparisons, dropout, sharpness, or example removal.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares CNN and FCN test performance on CIFAR-10 and constructed MNIST sequence tasks, and varies locality to investigate V3's proposed mechanism. Its theoretical optimization results concern a related question rather than image-classification test error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the central conclusion: locality can give CNNs and LCNs a computational advantage over FCNs. Qualify FCN failure as concerning hard local parity instances under the stated initialization assumptions, rather than every local pattern. Empirically, the advantage reverses for short nonlocal MNIST sequences, and all architectures perform poorly on long nonlocal sequences.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic parity tasks, theoretical optimization analysis, and sequence-based MNIST experiments rather than the natural-label image-classification recipe in V3. It uses AdaDelta for the MNIST experiments and RMSprop for the CIFAR-10 comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The architecture comparison changes with whether the parity pattern is local or nonconsecutive; the FCN result also depends on sequence length. The text reports LCN outperforming CNN on the local-parity task.

fits_no_version.finding: CNNs have polynomial-time learning guarantees for local binary k-patterns; FCNs have very small initial gradients for a hard parity instance under permutation-invariant initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local architectural bias can create a computational learning advantage on local binary pattern tasks under specified initialization and gradient-descent assumptions.

record.problems: The experiments use constructed parity labels rather than natural labels. The reported architecture results are qualitative in the text, without exact accuracy values or uncertainty estimates. The theoretical FCN failure depends on stated initialization and task assumptions.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold under converged training.

CIFAR-100 and SVHN comparisons; fully connected networks learning sparse local connections; initialization from trained convolutional networks. The MNIST experiments use constructed parity labels rather than ordinary digit labels.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or switching optimizers.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V3. The supplied text supports qualitative comparisons but not precise plotted accuracies or uncertainty estimates. The record's gate note misidentifies R7 as the CIFAR-10 comparison; that comparison is R6.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.

The experiments use synthetic parity labels on MNIST sequences and CIFAR-10, not the full set of image datasets named in the version; they do not test learned sparse connections or convolutional initialization of fully connected networks.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons and their tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to training-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
